question: Which one of these is NOT an igneous rock?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dolomite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dolomite** is a sedimentary rock, not an igneous rock.
 
• Igneous rocks are formed from the solidification of molten magma or lava and include rocks like **Granite**, **Diorite**, and **Basalt**.
 
• **Granite** is a common example of an intrusive igneous rock.
 
• **Diorite** is an intrusive igneous rock composed mainly of plagioclase feldspar, biotite, hornblende, and/or pyroxene.
 
• **Basalt** is an extrusive igneous rock formed from the rapid cooling of basaltic lava exposed at or very near the surface of a planet or moon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dolomite** is primarily composed of the mineral dolomite (CaMg(CO3)2).
 
• It is commonly found in sedimentary basins worldwide and forms from the alteration of limestone or lime mud and can also form from the precipitation of calcium and magnesium carbonates in marine and freshwater environments.
 
• Dolomite is used in various industries including construction (as a building stone and crushed stone), agriculture (as a soil conditioner and feed additive for livestock), and in the chemical industry (for the production of magnesium and calcium salts).
 
• Understanding the differences between rock types is essential in geology, mining, and various engineering fields.
